title: Evenepoel Wins Tour de France Time Trial, Cuts Into Pogačar's Overall Lead
excerpt: The Belgian world time trial champion clocked 32 minutes and 19 seconds over the 26.1 km Stage 16 course on Belgium's national holiday, shaving 28 seconds off Tadej Pogačar's commanding advantage.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Remco Evenepoel won Stage 16 time trial, finishing 28 seconds ahead of Tadej Pogačar.
  • Pogačar's overall lead is now 4 minutes and 32 seconds with five stages left.
  • Evenepoel's teammate Florian Lipowitz crashed and was hospitalized with a suspected shoulder injury.
  • This victory marks Evenepoel's fourth Tour stage win and third in time trials.

  • Remco Evenepoel won the Stage 16 individual time trial of the 2026 Tour de France in 32 minutes and 19 seconds, finishing 28 seconds ahead of overall leader Tadej Pogačar.
  • Pogačar's overall lead is now 4 minutes and 32 seconds over Evenepoel, with five stages remaining before the race ends Sunday in Paris.
  • Evenepoel's Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe teammate Florian Lipowitz crashed out on a sharp bend and was taken to hospital with a suspected shoulder injury; he had been fifth in the general classification.
  • The victory was Evenepoel's fourth Tour stage win overall and his third in time trials — marking the third consecutive year he has won a time trial at the Tour de France.

Evenepoel Dominates the Only Time Trial

Remco Evenepoel delivered a commanding performance in the only individual time trial of this year's Tour de France on Tuesday, blasting through the 26.1-kilometer Stage 16 course from Évian-les-Bains to Thonon-les-Bains in 32 minutes and 19 seconds.

The route along the shores of Lake Geneva featured a 16.4-kilometer Category 2 climb up the Côte de Larringes followed by a technical descent and a flat run into the finish. From the first intermediate checkpoint, it was clear Evenepoel was riding at a different level. At the third checkpoint in Thonon-les-Bains, he led Pogačar by 16 seconds and Danish rider Mattias Skjelmose by 56 seconds.

When the dust settled, Skjelmose of Lidl-Trek took third at 1 minute and 4 seconds behind Evenepoel, while Paul Seixas of Decathlon-AG2R finished fourth and Isaac Del Toro of UAE Team Emirates XRG rounded out the top five.

> **""Tadej is on his way to win a fifth Tour de France," he said."**

"I think it was a really good execution from start to finish, he had good control."

— Klaas Lodewyck, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe Sporting Director

A Bittersweet Belgian National Day

The Stage 16 victory carried special significance for Evenepoel. July 21 is Belgium's national holiday, and his entire family — parents, wife, and in-laws — were in attendance. It was also his second consecutive stage win after taking Stage 15's mountain finish on Sunday, where he outsprinted Pogačar to the line at the Plateau de Solaison.

"On the Belgian national day is pretty special — I read this morning it's been a while since Belgium won on National Day, so I'm proud to be the one."

— Remco Evenepoel

The triumph was Evenepoel's fourth Tour stage victory overall and his third in time trials, continuing a streak that has seen the world and Olympic time trial champion dominate the discipline at the Tour for three consecutive years.

Lipowitz Crash Clouds Team's Celebration

The celebrations were tempered by the crash of Evenepoel's Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe teammate Florian Lipowitz. The German rider, who had been fifth in the general classification and posted the fourth-fastest time through the three intermediate checkpoints, lost control on a sharp right-hand bend near the 19.8-kilometer mark and slid into the sidewalk kerb.

Lipowitz was escorted to a medical vehicle holding his left arm, with a suspected shoulder injury forcing him out of the race. The crash came just two days after two-time former Tour winner Jonas Vingegaard was also forced to abandon the race following a crash on Stage 15 that left him with a fractured collarbone requiring surgery.

"That's very unfortunate, it's like a bittersweet pill to swallow with this victory. I will really miss him for the whole week."

— Remco Evenepoel, on teammate Lipowitz's crash

Pogačar himself had a wobble navigating the same treacherous corner but managed to stay upright and continue.

The Overall Picture: Pogačar Still in Command

Despite Evenepoel's gains, four-time Tour champion Pogačar remains firmly in control of the yellow jersey. His 4-minute-32-second advantage — down from 5 minutes before Stage 15 — is substantial with five stages remaining. Del Toro sits third at 6 minutes and 51 seconds, while Seixas is fourth at 7 minutes and 11 seconds.

Evenepoel himself acknowledged the reality of the situation. "Tadej is on his way to win a fifth Tour de France," he said. "I think it's just amazing that I can be a bit close to him. It's an honor to race with him."

A fifth Tour crown would place the 27-year-old Slovenian alongside Belgium's Eddy Merckx, Spain's Miguel Indurain, and French riders Jacques Anquetil and Bernard Hinault — the only riders to have won the race five times.

What's Next

Stage 17 on Wednesday takes the peloton from Chambéry to Voiron over 174.7 kilometers. With the Alps providing the backdrop for the final decisive mountain stages, Evenepoel will look to chip away further at Pogačar's advantage, though overturning a deficit of more than four minutes against the dominant Slovenian remains an enormous challenge. The race concludes Sunday in Paris.
